tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session navigated to the Magento admin Online Customers page, authenticated, dismissed a modal, inspected the grid header and filter row layout, populated filters (ID from/to, First Name, Email, Session Start range, Last Activity range, Type select, Last URL), and applied the Search action. The IP Address filter input was not present in the captured DOM and was therefore skipped; a presence-check is required when automating. Stable selectors were recorded using both elementHash values for elements the agent directly interacted with and header-relative XPath/CSS fallbacks for robustness.

Task Definition:
- Create a deterministic, reusable tool that: 1) opens the Magento Admin Online Customers grid (assumes authentication), 2) dismisses blocking modals, 3) fills provided filter values (ID ranges, names, email, optional IP, session/last-activity ranges, Type select, Last URL), 4) applies the Search filter, and 5) returns the filtered grid contents. The tool must include a presence-check for the IP Address filter (it can be absent) and use robust selectors to avoid strict-mode multi-element failures.

Action Plan (to-do list of necessary tool steps):
1) Navigate to the Online Customers grid URL.
2) Close the 'Incoming Message' modal if present (recorded click). 3) Wait for the filter row to render. 4) Populate ID From/To input fields. 5) Populate name/email/last URL inputs and date range inputs. 6) Select Type option if provided. 7) Run an IP-presence check and populate IP if the input exists (agentic step). 8) Click Search to apply filters. 9) Wait for grid refresh. 10) Extract the grid rows and pagination/total records information and return as structured output.

Variable Identification (tool inputs):
- id_from, id_to (ID range)  
- first_name, middle_name, last_name (name filters)  
- email  
- ip_address (optional; presence-checked at runtime)  
- session_start_from, session_start_to (date/time strings in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)  
- last_activity_from, last_activity_to (date/time strings)  
- type (select option; accepts 'Customer'/'Visitor' or recorded values 'c'/'v')  
- last_url  
- per_page (optional rows per page setting)
All above are optional so callers can set only the filters they need.

Step Optimization and Robustness:
- Use direct navigation to the known admin URL rather than clicking through menus.  
- Use recorded deterministic elementHash values for elements the agent already interacted with (these resolve to single elements in the test run).  
- For elements that may be absent or dynamic (most notably the IP Address filter), use an 'agent' step to probe the DOM and act accordingly to avoid strict-mode selector errors.  
- Prefer header-text-anchored XPath or JS queries as fallbacks (document.evaluate on the table that contains the 'IP Address' header) to compute the correct column and then target the filter cell.  
- Include waits after closing modals and after clicking Search to avoid interacting while overlays/ajax loaders are visible.  
- The tool intentionally avoids authentication steps (the recorded session authenticated earlier). If a login screen appears, the automation should be run in a context where login is already completed.

Deterministic guarantees and constraints:
- All click/input/select steps use either an elementHash recorded from the session (stable for this environment) or an agentic DOM probe to avoid ambiguous multi-element matches.  
- The IP Address filter is explicitly checked before use; the tool will not attempt to type into a non-existent element.  
- Extraction step returns structured grid data so the caller can confirm the results.  

Omitted or non-essential steps (by design):
- No global authentication or navigation to other admin sections is included.  
- No additional filtering/sorting iterations beyond applying the provided filters and extracting results.  

This tool therefore provides a single-purpose, deterministic automation to apply the Online Customers filters and return the resulting grid, with safety checks and fallbacks for the IP Address input and modal overlays.
name: magento_online_customers_filter_tool
description: Automate applying filters on the Magento Admin 'Online Customers' grid and extract resulting grid data. The tool assumes an authenticated Magento admin session is already available in the browser context. It uses recorded stable element hashes and header-relative selectors as fallbacks, includes a presence-check for the IP Address filter (which may be missing in some installations), and returns the filtered grid contents.

steps.description: Navigate to the Magento Admin Online Customers grid (assumes active authenticated admin session).
Dismiss the 'Incoming Message' modal if present (close button recorded). This click is safe to run even if the modal is not present.
Allow the grid and filter row to render and any overlay to disappear.
Set ID 'From' value (first part of ID range filter).
Set ID 'To' value (second part of ID range filter).
Select the 'Type' dropdown option. Accepts visible label (e.g., 'Customer') or option value (e.g., 'c'). If {type} is empty, the recorded select is not changed.

Some Magento setups omit the IP Address filter input. This agentic step will check the DOM for the IP filter cell (column 'IP Address') and set its input if found. It must not throw an error if the cell is missing.
steps.task: Verify the IP Address filter cell exists and, if present, set the IP address value to {ip_address}; otherwise record that the IP filter is absent.

steps.description: Click the Search button to apply filters (recorded Search button element hash).
Wait for the grid to refresh after applying filters.
Return the grid rows and metadata after filters are applied so the caller can confirm filters took effect.
steps.goal: Extract the filtered grid results: capture column headers, each visible row as structured objects (ID, First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Email, IP Address, Session Start Time, Last Activity, Type, Last URL), and total records count.

input_schema.name: id_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound for the numeric ID filter (use numeric string). Example: "100"

input_schema.name: id_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound for the numeric ID filter (use numeric string). Example: "200"

input_schema.name: first_name
input_schema.description: First name filter value (partial or full). Example: "John"

input_schema.name: middle_name
input_schema.description: Middle name filter value (partial or full).

input_schema.name: last_name
input_schema.description: Last name filter value (partial or full).

input_schema.name: email
input_schema.description: Email address to filter by. Example: "john.doe@example.com"

input_schema.name: ip_address
input_schema.description: IP address to filter by (IPv4 or IPv6). Note: the IP filter input may not exist in some Magento setups; the tool checks presence before filling.

input_schema.name: session_start_from
input_schema.description: Session Start Time 'From' value in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' format. Example: "2026-02-01 00:00:00"

input_schema.name: session_start_to
input_schema.description: Session Start Time 'To' value in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' format. Example: "2026-02-02 23:59:59"

input_schema.name: last_activity_from
input_schema.description: Last Activity 'From' value in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' format.

input_schema.name: last_activity_to
input_schema.description: Last Activity 'To' value in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' format.

input_schema.name: type
input_schema.description: Type filter option. Use visible label (e.g., 'Customer' or 'Visitor') or the select option value (recorded value 'c' for Customer). If left empty, the tool will not change the Type filter.

input_schema.name: last_url
input_schema.description: Last URL filter (partial or full). Example: "/checkout/cart"

input_schema.name: per_page
input_schema.description: Optional rows-per-page value for the grid (20,30,50,100,200). If provided, the tool will attempt to set the per-page select in the pager.
